payload.body:
## Context

Hack now has a clearer split between host-side env injection (`hack host exec` / `hack host shell`) and one-off compose-network execution (`hack run <service> ...`). There is still no first-class Hack command for running inside an already-running service container.

## Goals

- Add a top-level `hack exec <service> ...` surface for commands that should run inside a live container.
- Preserve explicit service selection and avoid guessing execution context.
- Document the difference between `hack host`, `hack run`, and `hack exec`.

## Notes

Current fallback is raw `docker compose exec <service> ...`, which is functional but breaks the otherwise consistent Hack command model.

## Links

- Follow-up from host command UX work on 2026-04-01
payload.title: Add first-class hack exec for already-running service containers

payload.body:
## Context

The lifecycle stop-path fix now interrupts tmux-backed lifecycle windows before killing the session, which cleared the active `event-agent` main-session tunnel listeners on 2026-04-01.

Residual orphaned `session-manager-plugin` processes were still visible from older `event-agent` branch sessions and other non-main process groups after the main session was cleaned up.

## Goals

- Audit lifecycle teardown for branch sessions and non-tmux backends.
- Confirm whether stale process groups can remain after prior hard session kills.
- Add a targeted cleanup or recovery path if those residual children are still possible.

## Notes

Observed residual process groups included older `connect-local-dev.sh` / `session-manager-plugin` trees even after the main `event-agent--lifecycle` session was removed.
payload.title: Follow up lifecycle teardown for branch and non-tmux sessions

payload.body:
## Context
While validating Hack lifecycle cleanup against `/Users/hack/dev/external/TeamSidewinder/event-agent`, the stale tunnel tree that remained on the machine was rooted in a manually run `bun run proxy` process under the plain `event-agent` tmux session, not in a `--lifecycle` tmux session.

## Goals
- Determine whether Hack should detect and warn about stale manual `proxy` trees when `hack ps` shows no active compose services.
- Decide whether workspace/session commands need an optional cleanup path for known host-side helper processes.
- Avoid conflating this with lifecycle-managed process cleanup.

## Notes
- Observed process group root: `bun run proxy` with descendant `scripts/connect-local-dev.sh` and six `session-manager-plugin` listeners on 3306/9200/9201/8443/8444/8445.
- Parent process chain pointed at a Codex-started host session, not a Hack lifecycle session.
- The new lifecycle fix successfully cleaned a fresh `event-agent--lifecycle-lifecycle-cleanup-check` session, so this is a separate gap.

## Links
- Repo: `/Users/hack/dev/hack-dance/hack`
- External repo under test: `/Users/hack/dev/external/TeamSidewinder/event-agent`
payload.title: Investigate event-agent manual proxy cleanup outside lifecycle

payload.body:
## Context
We reduced repeated sudo prompts for dnsmasq/cache repair by adding a one-time `hack global authorize` path, but crash recovery is still incomplete when the Docker backend itself dies. The user-facing pain is that Hack can restart its own daemon and now recover DNS more cleanly, but it still cannot automatically bring OrbStack/Docker and the global stack back after backend failures.

## Goals
- Detect Docker Desktop/OrbStack backend death distinctly from ordinary project/container failures.
- Design a one-time authorization/install path, if needed, so recovery does not block on repeated sudo/admin prompts.
- Let Hack or hackd recover the backend app and then re-run global runtime recovery (`hack global up` equivalent) safely.
- Define clear limits so we do not silently restart host-level software in unsafe situations.

## Notes
- Related current work: passwordless DNS recovery via `hack global authorize`.
- Likely intersects with existing crash-capture and daemon self-heal work.
- Should decide whether this belongs in hackd, a launchd helper, a privileged helper, or explicit operator-approved repair commands.

## Links
- src/commands/global.ts
- tests/global-command.macos.test.ts
payload.title: Add privileged macOS runtime recovery for Docker/OrbStack + global infra

payload.body:
## Context
Hack now has a working Homebrew formula in `hack-dance/homebrew-tap`, but each new release still requires a manual formula version + checksum update.

## Goals
- Define how the release pipeline should update `hack-dance/homebrew-tap/Formula/hack.rb`
- Avoid shipping new Hack releases without a matching brew install path
- Keep the tap README and formula version in sync with the latest release

## Notes
Current formula targets the v2.3.0 release tarballs and wraps `hack` with `HACK_ASSETS_DIR` so bundled assets work under Homebrew.

## Links
- Repo: hack-dance/hack
- Tap: hack-dance/homebrew-tap
payload.title: Automate Homebrew tap updates on release

## Context
Full `bun x ultracite check` now passes with no errors, but the repo still has 81 complexity warnings concentrated in older auth/dispatch/node/supervisor paths.

## Goals
- Reduce or eliminate the remaining `lint/complexity/noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity` warnings.
- Keep behavior unchanged while extracting helpers and narrowing responsibilities.

## Notes
- Examples called out by Ultracite include `src/commands/dispatch.ts`, `src/commands/node.ts`, `src/commands/global.ts`, `src/control-plane/extensions/github/auth.ts`, and several `services/auth-broker` modules.
- This is follow-up cleanup, not a release blocker.

## Links
- Commit: 939c2b2c
payload.title: Reduce remaining Ultracite complexity warnings
